高さ10m |埋葬施設 = [[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = 副葬品多数・[[須恵器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]中葉 |被葬者 = |陵墓 = |史跡 = 若狭町指定史跡「丸山古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土品（福井県指定有形文化財） |特記事項 = 円墳としては若狭地方第1位の規模
墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Fukui |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 丸山塚古墳 |ラベル位置 = bottom }} '''丸山塚古墳'''（まるやまづかこふん、丸山古墳）は、[[福井県]][[三方上中郡]][[若狭町]]天徳寺にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。上中古墳群（うち天徳寺古墳群）を構成した古墳の1つ。若狭町指定史跡に指定され（指定名称は「丸山古墳」）、出土品は福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている（指定名称は「丸山古墳出土品」）。 若狭地方では円墳としては最大規模の古墳であったが、現在では失われている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+上中古墳群の主な古墳 !古墳群!!古墳名!!形状!!墳丘長!!築造時期 |- |脇袋||[[上ノ塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||100m||5c初 |- | ||城山古墳||前方後円墳||63m||5c中 |- |rowspan=2|脇袋||[[西塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||74m||5c後 |- |[[中塚古墳 (若狭町)|中塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||72m||5c末 |- |天徳寺||[[十善の森古墳]]||前方後円墳||68m||6c初 |- |rowspan=2|日笠||[[上船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||70m||6c前 |- |[[下船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||85m||6c中 |- |天徳寺||'''丸山塚古墳'''||円墳||50m||6c中 |}
福井県南西部、若狭地方中央部において[[北川]]左岸にあった大型円墳である。南250メートルには[[十善の森古墳]]が所在し、天徳寺古墳群を形成した。[[1957年]]（[[昭和]]32年）に北川水害復旧工事で復旧用土として用いるため、石室内の調査後に破壊されている。 墳形は円形で、直径約50メートル・高さ約10メートルを測った。墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘表面で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘周囲には幅20メートルの周濠が巡らされた{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。埋葬施設は片袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南東方向に開口した{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。玄室長6メートル・羨道長11メートルにおよぶ大型石室であり、石室内は盗掘に遭っていたが、調査では画文帯神獣鏡・装身具・武器・武具・馬具・[[須恵器]]など多数が検出されている。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃と推定される『若狭三方縄文博物館・若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録』 若狭町歴史文化課、2014年（若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録セクション）。{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。若狭地方最後の前方後円墳である[[下船塚古墳]]に後続する時期に位置づけられ、前方後円墳から円墳へ転換後の大首長の存在を示唆する古墳になる。全国的に首長墓は前方後円墳から円墳・方墳へと転換し、巨大な石材を用いた横穴式石室が構築されるようになるが、若狭地方ではその転換が早く、[[ヤマト政権]]との密接な関係が指摘される。 古墳域は[[1955年]]（昭和30年）に旧上中町指定史跡（現在は若狭町指定史跡）に指定され、出土品は[[1978年]]（昭和53年）に福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている。 === 来歴 === * [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）、[[昭和28年台風第13号|台風13号]]による大水害、北川堤防の決壊。 * [[1955年]]（昭和30年）12月6日、旧上中町指定史跡に指定（現在は若狭町指定史跡）。 * [[1957年]]（昭和32年）、北川水害復旧工事に伴う石室内調査。調査後に石室の爆破破壊、墳丘削平（上中町教育委員会、[[1970年]]に報告）。 * [[1978年]]（昭和53年）7月25日、出土品が福井県指定有形文化財に指定。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては片袖式[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南東方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}。 * 玄室：長さ6メートル、幅約3メートル、高さ4.3メートル * 羨道：長さ約11メートル、幅1.5メートル == 出土品 == [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 双鳳環頭・三葉環頭.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|双鳳環頭・三葉環頭
（福井県指定有形文化財）}}{{small|若狭町教育委員会蔵、大阪歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] 石室内から出土した副葬品は次の通り[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 画文帯神獣鏡ほか（丸山塚古墳出土）]（福井県ホームページ「福井の文化財」）。。 * 銅鏡 ** 画文帯神獣鏡 1 * 装身具 ** 勾玉 1 ** 丸玉 7 ** 小玉 10 * 武器類 ** 挂甲 1 ** 刀身片 若干 ** 環頭柄頭 2 ** 刀装具残片 若干 ** 水晶三輪玉 1 ** 鉄鏃 11 * 武具 ** 衝角付冑 1 * 馬具 ** 鞍金具片 若干 ** 杏葉 9 * [[須恵器]]片その他 若干 石室内は盗掘に遭っていたため、副葬品の全容は明らかでない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 == 文化財 == === 福井県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 丸山古墳出土品（考古資料） - 所有者は若狭町。1978年（昭和53年）7月25日指定。 === 若狭町指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 丸山古墳 - 1955年（昭和30年）12月6日指定。 == 関連施設 == * 若狭町歴史文化館（若狭町市場） == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} ==参考文献== {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1981|chapter=|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 18 福井県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490182|ref={{Harvid|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=山口充|year=1989|chapter=丸山塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} ==関連文献== {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1970|chapter=丸山塚古墳|title=若狭上中町の古墳|publisher=上中町教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[十善の森古墳]] == 外部リンク == * [https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 画文帯神獣鏡ほか（丸山塚古墳出土）] - 福井県ホームページ「福井の文化財」 * [http://www1.city.obama.fukui.jp/japan_heritage/bunkazai/detail.php 小浜市・若狭町日本遺産活用推進協議会「日本遺産 御食国若狭と鯖街道」] {{DEFAULTSORT:まるやまつかこふん わかさちよう}} [[Category:福井県の古墳]] [[Category:若狭町の歴史]] [[Category:円墳]] [[Category:福井県内の市町村指定史跡]] [[Category:福井県指定有形文化財]]

墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Fukui |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 丸山塚古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''丸山塚古墳'''（まるやまづかこふん、丸山古墳）は、[[福井県]][[三方上中郡]][[若狭町]]天徳寺にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。上中古墳群（うち天徳寺古墳群）を構成した古墳の1つ。若狭町指定史跡に指定され（指定名称は「丸山古墳」）、出土品は福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている（指定名称は「丸山古墳出土品」）。 若狭地方では円墳としては最大規模の古墳であったが、現在では失われている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+上中古墳群の主な古墳 !古墳群!!古墳名!!形状!!墳丘長!!築造時期 |- |脇袋||[[上ノ塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||100m||5c初 |- | ||城山古墳||前方後円墳||63m||5c中 |- |rowspan=2|脇袋||[[西塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||74m||5c後 |- |[[中塚古墳 (若狭町)|中塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||72m||5c末 |- |天徳寺||[[十善の森古墳]]||前方後円墳||68m||6c初 |- |rowspan=2|日笠||[[上船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||70m||6c前 |- |[[下船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||85m||6c中 |- |天徳寺||'''丸山塚古墳'''||円墳||50m||6c中 |}
福井県南西部、若狭地方中央部の[[北川]]左岸に築造された大型円墳である。南250メートルには[[十善の森古墳]]が所在し、天徳寺古墳群を形成した。[[1957年]]（[[昭和]]32年）に北川水害復旧工事で復旧用土として用いるため、石室内の調査後に破壊されている。 墳形は円形で、直径約50メートル・高さ約10メートルを測った。墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘表面で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘周囲には幅20メートルの周濠が巡らされた{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。埋葬施設は片袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南東方向に開口した{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。玄室長6メートル・羨道長11メートルにおよぶ大型石室であり、石室内は盗掘に遭っていたが、調査では画文帯神獣鏡・装身具・武器・武具・馬具・[[須恵器]]など多数が検出されている。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃と推定される『若狭三方縄文博物館・若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録』 若狭町歴史文化課、2014年（若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録セクション）。{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。若狭地方最後の前方後円墳である[[下船塚古墳]]に後続する時期に位置づけられ、前方後円墳から円墳へ転換後の大首長の存在を示唆する古墳になる。全国的に首長墓は前方後円墳から円墳・方墳へと転換し、巨大な石材を用いた横穴式石室が構築されるようになるが、若狭地方ではその転換が早く、[[ヤマト政権]]との密接な関係が指摘される。 古墳域は[[1955年]]（昭和30年）に旧上中町指定史跡（現在は若狭町指定史跡）に指定され、出土品は[[1978年]]（昭和53年）に福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている。 === 来歴 === * [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）、[[昭和28年台風第13号|台風13号]]による大水害、北川堤防の決壊。 * [[1955年]]（昭和30年）12月6日、旧上中町指定史跡に指定（現在は若狭町指定史跡）。 * [[1957年]]（昭和32年）、北川水害復旧工事に伴う石室内調査。調査後に石室の爆破破壊、墳丘削平（上中町教育委員会、[[1970年]]に報告）。 * [[1978年]]（昭和53年）7月25日、出土品が福井県指定有形文化財に指定。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては片袖式[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南東方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}。 * 玄室：長さ6メートル、幅約3メートル、高さ4.3メートル * 羨道：長さ約11メートル、幅1.5メートル == 出土品 == [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 双鳳環頭・三葉環頭.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|双鳳環頭・三葉環頭

（福井県指定有形文化財）}}{{small|若狭町教育委員会蔵、大阪歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] 石室内から出土した副葬品は次の通り[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 画文帯神獣鏡ほか（丸山塚古墳出土）]（福井県ホームページ「福井の文化財」）。。 * 銅鏡 ** 画文帯神獣鏡 1 * 装身具 ** 勾玉 1 ** 丸玉 7 ** 小玉 10 * 武器類 ** 挂甲 1 ** 刀身片 若干 ** 環頭柄頭 2 ** 刀装具残片 若干 ** 水晶三輪玉 1 ** 鉄鏃 11 * 武具 ** 衝角付冑 1 * 馬具 ** 鞍金具片 若干 ** 杏葉 9 * [[須恵器]]片その他 若干 石室内は盗掘に遭っていたため、副葬品の全容は明らかでない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 == 文化財 == === 福井県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 丸山古墳出土品（考古資料） - 所有者は若狭町。1978年（昭和53年）7月25日指定。 === 若狭町指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 丸山古墳 - 1955年（昭和30年）12月6日指定。 == 関連施設 == * 若狭町歴史文化館（若狭町市場） == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} ==参考文献== {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1981|chapter=|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 18 福井県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490182|ref={{Harvid|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=山口充|year=1989|chapter=丸山塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} ==関連文献== {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1970|chapter=丸山塚古墳|title=若狭上中町の古墳|publisher=上中町教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[十善の森古墳]] == 外部リンク == * [https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 画文帯神獣鏡ほか（丸山塚古墳出土）] - 福井県ホームページ「福井の文化財」 * [http://www1.city.obama.fukui.jp/japan_heritage/bunkazai/detail.php 小浜市・若狭町日本遺産活用推進協議会「日本遺産 御食国若狭と鯖街道」] {{DEFAULTSORT:まるやまつかこふん わかさちよう}} [[Category:福井県の古墳]] [[Category:若狭町の歴史]] [[Category:円墳]] [[Category:福井県内の市町村指定史跡]] [[Category:福井県指定有形文化財]]

墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Fukui |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 丸山塚古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''丸山塚古墳'''（まるやまづかこふん、丸山古墳）は、[[福井県]][[三方上中郡]][[若狭町]]天徳寺にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。上中古墳群（うち天徳寺古墳群）を構成した古墳の1つ。若狭町指定史跡に指定され（指定名称は「丸山古墳」）、出土品は福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている（指定名称は「丸山古墳出土品」）。 若狭地方では円墳としては最大規模の古墳であったが、現在では失われている。 == 概要 ==

墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Fukui |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 丸山塚古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''丸山塚古墳'''（まるやまづかこふん、丸山古墳）は、[[福井県]][[三方上中郡]][[若狭町]]天徳寺にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。上中古墳群（うち天徳寺古墳群）を構成した古墳の1つ。若狭町指定史跡に指定され（指定名称は「丸山古墳」）、出土品は福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている（指定名称は「丸山古墳出土品」）。 若狭地方では円墳としては最大規模の古墳であったが、現在では失われている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+上中古墳群の主な古墳 !古墳群!!古墳名!!形状!!墳丘長!!築造時期 |- |脇袋||[[上ノ塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||100m||5c初 |- | ||城山古墳||前方後円墳||63m||5c中 |- |rowspan=2|脇袋||[[西塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||74m||5c後 |- |[[中塚古墳 (若狭町)|中塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||72m||5c末 |- |天徳寺||[[十善の森古墳]]||前方後円墳||68m||6c初 |- |rowspan=2|日笠||[[上船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||70m||6c前 |- |[[下船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||85m||6c中 |- |天徳寺||'''丸山塚古墳'''||円墳||50m||6c中 |}
福井県南西部、若狭地方中央部の[[北川]]左岸に築造された大型円墳である。南250メートルには[[十善の森古墳]]が所在し、天徳寺古墳群を形成した。[[1957年]]（[[昭和]]32年）に北川水害復旧工事で復旧用土として用いるため、石室内の調査後に破壊されている。 墳形は円形で、直径約50メートル・高さ約10メートルを測った。墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘周囲には幅20メートルの周濠が巡らされた{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。埋葬施設は片袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南東方向に開口した{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。玄室長6メートル・羨道長11メートルにおよぶ大型石室であり、石室内は盗掘に遭っていたが、調査では画文帯神獣鏡・装身具・武器・武具・馬具・[[須恵器]]など多数が検出されている。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃と推定される『若狭三方縄文博物館・若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録』 若狭町歴史文化課、2014年（若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録セクション）。{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。若狭地方最後の前方後円墳である[[下船塚古墳]]に後続する時期に位置づけられ、前方後円墳から円墳へ転換後の大首長の存在を示唆する古墳になる。全国的に首長墓は前方後円墳から円墳・方墳へと転換し、巨大な石材を用いた横穴式石室が構築されるようになるが、若狭地方ではその転換が早く、[[ヤマト政権]]との密接な関係が指摘される。 古墳域は[[1955年]]（昭和30年）に旧上中町指定史跡（現在は若狭町指定史跡）に指定され、出土品は[[1978年]]（昭和53年）に福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）、[[昭和28年台風第13号|台風13号]]による大水害、北川堤防の決壊。 * [[1955年]]（昭和30年）12月6日、旧上中町指定史跡に指定（現在は若狭町指定史跡）。 * [[1957年]]（昭和32年）、北川水害復旧工事に伴う石室内調査。調査後に石室の爆破破壊、墳丘削平（上中町教育委員会、[[1970年]]に報告）。 * [[1978年]]（昭和53年）7月25日、出土品が福井県指定有形文化財に指定。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては片袖式[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南東方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}。 * 玄室：長さ6メートル、幅約3メートル、高さ4.3メートル * 羨道：長さ約11メートル、幅1.5メートル == 出土品 == [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 画文帯神獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|画文帯神獣鏡}}{{small|[[花園大学歴史博物館]]企画展示時に撮影。}}]] [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 双鳳環頭・三葉環頭.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|双鳳環頭・三葉環頭}}{{small|大阪歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 武器・武具.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|武器・武具}}{{small|花園大学歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 馬具.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|馬具}}{{small|花園大学歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Tumulus| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!Name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Kami no Tsuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishi Tsuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Naka Tsuka Kofun (Wakasa Town)|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Tumulus||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments * Magatama (curved beads) x 1 * Round beads x 7 * Small beads x 10 * Weaponry * Armor fragments * Blade fragments * Hilt decorations x 2 * Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 * Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor * Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings * Saddle fittings * Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} fragments File:Maruyamazuka Kofun 玉類.jpg|Ornaments File:Maruyamazuka Kofun 衝角付冑.jpg|Helmet File:Maruyamazuka Kofun 楕円形杏葉.jpg|Elliptical horse ornaments File:Maruyamazuka Kofun 剣菱形杏葉.jpg|Kusaragi-shaped horse ornaments File:Maruyamazuka Kofun 鐘形杏葉.jpg|Bell-shaped horse ornaments File:Maruyamazuka Kofun 須恵器.jpg|Sue ware == Cultural Properties == === Fukui Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties * Excavated artifacts from Maruyama Kofun (archaeological materials) – Designated July 25, 1978. === Wakasa Town Designated Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites * Maruyama The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * {{ill|Mirror with trifoil beads x 1 * Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor * Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings * Saddle fittings * Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Tumulus| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Tumulus||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_category/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments * Magatama (curved beads) x 1 * Round beads x 7 * Small beads x 10 * Weaponry * Armor fragments * Blade fragments * Hilt decorations x 2 * Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 * Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor * Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings * Saddle fittings * Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * 2 * Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 * Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor * Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings * Saddle fittings * Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the Site of the kofun| Alternate name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| Coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| Shape=Round Tumulus (円墳)| Size=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| Burial Facility={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}| Excavated Artifacts=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Cultural Properties=Excavated artifacts designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties| Special Notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Tumulus| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Tumulus||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Burial Mound)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width approx. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length approx. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors * {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments * Magatama (curved beads) x 1 * Round beads x 7 * Small beads x 10 * Weaponry * Armor fragments * Blade fragments * Hilt decorations x 2 * Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 * Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor * Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings * Saddle fittings * Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土
