Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

{{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Otheruses||{{ill|Kofun in Wakasa Town, Uryu|ja|若狭町瓜生にある古墳}} (Jōge no Mori Kofun)|{{ill|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Wakibukuro)|ja|脇袋丸山塚古墳}}}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}| name=Maruyamazuka Kofun| image=[[File:Maruyamazuka Kofun (Wakasa), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Site of the kofun| Alternate name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| Coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| Shape=Round Kofun (円墳)| Size=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| Burial Facility={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| Excavated Artifacts=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Cultural Properties=Excavated artifacts designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties| Special Notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} Site of the kofun| Alternate name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| Coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| Shape=Round Kofun (円墳)| Size=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| Burial Facility={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| Excavated Artifacts=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Cultural Properties=Excavated artifacts designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties| Special Notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 横矧板鋲留衝角付冑.JPG|Helmet 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張楕円形杏葉.JPG|Elliptical horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張剣菱形杏葉.JPG|Kusaragi-shaped horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張鐘形杏葉.JPG|Bell-shaped horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 須恵器.JPG|Sue pottery 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 須恵器 鈴付はそう.JPG|鈴付𤭯 == Cultural Properties == === Fukui Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Excavated artifacts from Maruyama Kofun (archaeological materials) – Designated July 25, 1978. === Wakasa Town Designated Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites ** Maruyama Kofun – Designated December 6, 1955. == Related Facilities == * Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum (Wakasa Town Market) == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Otheruses||{{ill|Kofun in Wakasa Town, Uryu|ja|若狭町瓜生にある古墳}} (Jōge no Mori Kofun)|{{ill|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Wakibukuro)|ja|脇袋丸山塚古墳}}}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}| name=Maruyamazuka Kofun| image=[[File:Maruyamazuka Kofun (Wakasa), gaikan.jpg|280px]]
Site of the kofun| Alternate name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| Coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| Shape=Round Kofun (円墳)| Size=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| Burial Facility={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| Excavated Artifacts=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Cultural Properties=Excavated artifacts designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties| Special Notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 横矧板鋲留衝角付冑.JPG|Helmet 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張楕円形杏葉.JPG|Elliptical horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張剣菱形杏葉.JPG|Kusaragi-shaped horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張鐘形杏葉.JPG|Bell-shaped horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 須恵器.JPG|Sue pottery 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 須恵器 鈴付はそう.JPG|鈴付𤭯 == Cultural Properties == === Fukui Prefecture Designated Height: 10 meters| Burial Facility={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| Excavated Artifacts=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Cultural Properties=Excavated artifacts designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties| Special Notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| Map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| Label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| Label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!Construction Period |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label Position=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Site of the kofun| alternate_name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| Shape=Round Kofun (円墳)| area=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| Burial Facility={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| Excavated Artifacts=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Cultural Properties=excavations designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties| Special Notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 横矧板鋲留衝角付冑.JPG|Helmet 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張楕円形杏葉.JPG|Elliptical horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張剣菱形杏葉.JPG|Kusaragi-shaped horse Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!Shape!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == Excavated Artifacts == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture Cultural Properties Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible Cultural Properties on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation on July 25. == Burial Facility == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the Site of the kofun| alternate_name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| type=Round Kofun (円墳)| area=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| burial={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| burial goods=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}| Historic Site Designation=Town-designated Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| other_designation=excavations designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation| notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous artifacts were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun Artifacts], Fukui Prefecture other_designation Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 横矧板鋲留衝角付冑.JPG|Helmet 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張楕円形杏葉.JPG|Elliptical horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張剣菱形杏葉.JPG|Kusaragi-shaped horse It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| Icon=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that formed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated artifacts are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it formed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the former Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now designated by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: Artifacts excavated from the kofun were designated as Fukui Prefecture Tangible other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * Burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters,
