Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now other_designation1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were other_designation1 as Fukui Prefecture other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now other_designation1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were other_designation1 as Fukui Prefecture other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now other_designation1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were other_designation1 as Fukui Prefecture other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture other_designation. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now other_designation1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were other_designation1 as Fukui Prefecture other_designation on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Height: 10 meters| burial={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| burial goods=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}| Historic Site =Town-Historic Site1 Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Historic Site=excavations Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site| notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring [[Category:pp error]]approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. Site of the kofun| alternate_name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}| coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| type=Round Kofun (円墳)| area=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| burial={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}| burial goods=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}| Historic Site =Town-Historic Site1 Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Historic Site=excavations Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site| notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** {{ill|Mirror with Deity and Beast Design|ja|画文帯神獣鏡}} * Ornaments ** Magatama (curved beads) x 1 ** Round beads x 7 ** Small beads x 10 * Weaponry ** Armor fragments ** Blade fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} fragments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|Ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 横矧板鋲留衝角付冑.JPG|Helmet 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張楕円形杏葉.JPG|Elliptical horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張剣菱形杏葉.JPG|Kusaragi-shaped horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 鉄地金銅張鐘形杏葉.JPG|Bell-shaped horse ornaments 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 須恵器.JPG|Sue pottery 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 須恵器 鈴付はそう.JPG|鈴付𤭯 == Historic Site == === Fukui Prefecture Designated Historic Site It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳|12=draft}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳|12=draft}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|12=draft}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|12=draft}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|12=draft}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳|12=draft}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
