The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the following[https://bunkazai.pref.fukui.lg.jp/search_Category:kk]][[Category:/content?detail_id=509-0 Maruyamazuka Kofun burial goods], Fukui Prefecture Historic Site Database.: * Bronze mirrors ** fragments ** Hilt decorations x 2 ** Water crystal trifoil beads x 1 ** Iron arrowheads x 11 * Armor ** Helmet with frontal ornament * Horse fittings ** Saddle fittings ** Ornaments x 9 * {{ill|Sue Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. 墳丘は非現存 |地図 = Japan Fukui |アイコン = 円墳 |ラベル = 丸山塚古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} '''丸山塚古墳'''（まるやまづかこふん、丸山古墳）は、[[福井県]][[三方上中郡]][[若狭町]]天徳寺にあった[[古墳]]。形状は[[円墳]]。上中古墳群（うち天徳寺古墳群）を構成した古墳の1つ。若狭町指定史跡に指定され（指定名称は「丸山古墳」）、出土品は福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている（指定名称は「丸山古墳出土品」）。 若狭地方では円墳としては最大規模の古墳であったが、現在では失われている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+上中古墳群の主な古墳 !古墳群!!古墳名!!形状!!墳丘長!!築造時期 |- |脇袋||[[上ノ塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||100m||5c初 |- | ||城山古墳||前方後円墳||63m||5c中 |- |rowspan=2|脇袋||[[西塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||74m||5c後 |- |[[中塚古墳 (若狭町)|中塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||72m||5c末 |- |天徳寺||[[十善の森古墳]]||前方後円墳||68m||6c初 |- |rowspan=2|日笠||[[上船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||70m||6c前 |- |[[下船塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||85m||6c中 |- |天徳寺||'''丸山塚古墳'''||円墳||50m||6c中 |}
福井県南西部、若狭地方中央部の[[北川]]左岸に築造された大型円墳である。南250メートルには[[十善の森古墳]]が所在し、天徳寺古墳群を形成した。[[1957年]]（[[昭和]]32年）に北川水害復旧工事で復旧用土として用いるため、石室内の調査後に破壊されている。 墳形は円形で、直径約50メートル・高さ約10メートルを測った。墳丘は2段築成{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘外表で[[葺石]]・[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。墳丘周囲には幅20メートルの周濠が巡らされた{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。埋葬施設は片袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南東方向に開口した{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。玄室長6メートル・羨道長11メートルにおよぶ大型石室であり、石室内は盗掘に遭っていたが、調査では画文帯神獣鏡・装身具・武器・武具・馬具・[[須恵器]]など多数が検出されている。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]中葉頃と推定される『若狭三方縄文博物館・若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録』 若狭町歴史文化課、2014年（若狭町歴史文化館常設展示図録セクション）。{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。若狭地方最後の前方後円墳である[[下船塚古墳]]に後続する時期に位置づけられ、前方後円墳から円墳へ転換後の大首長の存在を示唆する古墳になる。全国的に首長墓は前方後円墳から円墳・方墳へと転換し、巨大な石材を用いた横穴式石室が構築されるようになるが、若狭地方ではその転換が早く、[[ヤマト政権]]との密接な関係が指摘される。 古墳域は[[1955年]]（昭和30年）に旧上中町指定史跡（現在は若狭町指定史跡）に指定され、出土品は[[1978年]]（昭和53年）に福井県指定有形文化財に指定されている。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）、[[昭和28年台風第13号|台風13号]]による大水害、北川堤防の決壊。 * [[1955年]]（昭和30年）12月6日、旧上中町指定史跡に指定（現在は若狭町指定史跡）。 * [[1957年]]（昭和32年）、北川水害復旧工事に伴う石室内調査。調査後に石室の爆破破壊、墳丘削平（上中町教育委員会、[[1970年]]に報告）。 * [[1978年]]（昭和53年）7月25日、出土品が福井県指定有形文化財に指定。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては片袖式[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南東方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（平凡社）|1981}}。 * 玄室：長さ6メートル、幅約3メートル、高さ4.3メートル * 羨道：長さ約11メートル、幅1.5メートル == 出土品 == [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 画文帯神獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|画文帯神獣鏡}}{{small|[[花園大学歴史博物館]]企画展示時に撮影。}}]] [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 双鳳環頭・三葉環頭.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|双鳳環頭・三葉環頭}}{{small|大阪歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 武器・武具.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|武器・武具}}{{small|花園大学歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] [[ファイル:丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 馬具.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|馬具}}{{small|花園大学歴史博物館企画展示時に撮影。}}]] 若干 ** 環頭柄頭 2 ** 刀装具残片 若干 ** 水晶三輪玉 1 ** 鉄鏃 11 * 武具 ** 衝角付冑 1 * 馬具 ** 鞍金具片 若干 ** 杏葉 9 * [[須恵器]]片その他 若干 石室内は盗掘に遭っていたため、副葬品の全容は明らかでない{{Sfn|丸山塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}。 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 玉類.JPG|玉類 丸山塚古墳 (若狭町) 出土 The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|12=draft|12=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft|12=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=draft|12=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kita River (Fukui)|qq=}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|qq=}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Town|qq=}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikatakaminaka District|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukui Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

Site of the kofun| alternate_name=Maruyama Kofun| Cluster=Kami-naka Kofun Cluster (including Tentokuji Kofun Cluster)| location={{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Town|qq=}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikatakaminaka District|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukui Prefecture|qq=}}| coordinates={{Coord|35|27|59.70|N|135|50|44.78|E}}| type=Round Kofun (円墳)| area=Diameter: 50 meters
Height: 10 meters| burial={{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}| burial goods=Numerous grave goods, {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}}| Historic Site =Town-Historic Site1 Historic Site (Wakasa Town)| Historic Site=excavations Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site| notes=Largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region
Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} located in {{ill|Wakasa Town|ja|若狭町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Town|qq=}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District|ja|三方上中郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikatakaminaka District|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|ja|福井県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukui Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|ja|上ノ塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōnozuka Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|ja|西塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishizuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|上船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kita River (Fukui)|qq=}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|qq=}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width 1.5 meters == burial goods == Numerous burial goods were excavated from the stone chamber, including the It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River (Fukui)|ja|北川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kita River (Fukui)|qq=}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukiishi|qq=}} or {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|qq=}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|ja|下船塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|qq=}}, the last {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} in the region. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Wakasa, Fukui|Wakasa Town]], [[:en:Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Mikatakaminaka District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]], Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||[[:en:Jōnozuka Kofun|Jōnozuka Kofun]]||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||[[:en:Nishizuka Kofun|Nishizuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||[[:en:Kamifunazuka Kofun|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |[[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Wakasa, Fukui|Wakasa Town]], [[:en:Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Mikatakaminaka District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]], Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||[[:en:Jōnozuka Kofun|Jōnozuka Kofun]]||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||[[:en:Nishizuka Kofun|Nishizuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||[[:en:Kamifunazuka Kofun|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |[[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|qq=}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width
