Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Wakasa, Fukui|Wakasa Town]], [[:en:Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Mikatakaminaka District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]], Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||[[:en:Jōnozuka Kofun|Jōnozuka Kofun]]||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||[[:en:Nishizuka Kofun|Nishizuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||[[:en:Kamifunazuka Kofun|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |[[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Wakasa, Fukui|Wakasa Town]], [[:en:Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Mikatakaminaka District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]], Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||[[:en:Jōnozuka Kofun|Jōnozuka Kofun]]||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||[[:en:Nishizuka Kofun|Nishizuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||[[:en:Kamifunazuka Kofun|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |[[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Wakasa, Fukui|Wakasa Town]], [[:en:Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Mikatakaminaka District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]], Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||[[:en:Jōnozuka Kofun|Jōnozuka Kofun]]||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||[[:en:Nishizuka Kofun|Nishizuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||[[:en:Kamifunazuka Kofun|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |[[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==

The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Wakasa, Fukui|Wakasa Town]], [[:en:Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Mikatakaminaka District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]], Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||[[:en:Jōnozuka Kofun|Jōnozuka Kofun]]||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||[[:en:Nishizuka Kofun|Nishizuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||[[:en:Kamifunazuka Kofun|Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |[[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]]||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the [[:en:Kita River|Kita River (Fukui)]] in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of [[:en:Fukiishi|fukiishi]] or [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the [[:en:Shimofunazuka Kofun|Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun]], the last [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * [[:en:1953|1953]]: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * [[:en:1955|1955]]: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * [[:en:1957|1957]]: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * [[:en:1978|1978]]: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa, Fukui|en|Wakasa, Fukui|WD=Q1349039|lt=Wakasa Town}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|en|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|WD=Q1204541|lt=Mikatakaminaka District}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|WD=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|en|Jōnozuka Kofun|WD=Q17993480|lt=Jōnozuka Kofun}}||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|en|Nishizuka Kofun|WD=Q18337677|lt=Nishizuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifunazuka Kofun|en|Kamifunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17990214|lt=Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River|en|Kita River|WD=Q11401571|lt=Kita River (Fukui)}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} or {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}, the last {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * {{ill|1953|en|1953|WD=Q18585|lt=1953}}: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * {{ill|1955|en|1955|WD=Q18577|lt=1955}}: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * {{ill|1957|en|1957|WD=Q5311|lt=1957}}: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * {{ill|1978|en|1978|WD=Q2483|lt=1978}}: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|en|Jōnozuka Kofun|WD=Q17993480|lt=Jōnozuka Kofun}}||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|en|Nishizuka Kofun|WD=Q18337677|lt=Nishizuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifunazuka Kofun|en|Kamifunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17990214|lt=Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River|en|Kita River|WD=Q11401571|lt=Kita River (Fukui)}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} or {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}, the last {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * {{ill|1953|en|1953|WD=Q18585|lt=1953}}: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * {{ill|1955|en|1955|WD=Q18577|lt=1955}}: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * {{ill|1957|en|1957|WD=Q5311|lt=1957}}: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * {{ill|1978|en|1978|WD=Q2483|lt=1978}}: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}: * burial chamber: Length 6 meters, width a11rox. 3 meters, height 4.3 meters * Entrance passage: Length a11rox. 11 meters, width Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa, Fukui|en|Wakasa, Fukui|WD=Q1349039|lt=Wakasa Town}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|en|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|WD=Q1204541|lt=Mikatakaminaka District}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|WD=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|en|Jōnozuka Kofun|WD=Q17993480|lt=Jōnozuka Kofun}}||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|en|Nishizuka Kofun|WD=Q18337677|lt=Nishizuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifunazuka Kofun|en|Kamifunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17990214|lt=Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River|en|Kita River|WD=Q11401571|lt=Kita River (Fukui)}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} or {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}, the last {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * {{ill|1953|en|1953|WD=Q18585|lt=1953}}: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * {{ill|1955|en|1955|WD=Q18577|lt=1955}}: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * {{ill|1957|en|1957|WD=Q5311|lt=1957}}: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * {{ill|1978|en|1978|WD=Q2483|lt=1978}}: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River|en|Kita River|WD=Q11401571|lt=Kita River (Fukui)}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} or {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}, the last {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kinship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * {{ill|1953|en|1953|WD=Q18585|lt=1953}}: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * {{ill|1955|en|1955|WD=Q18577|lt=1955}}: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * {{ill|1957|en|1957|WD=Q5311|lt=1957}}: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * {{ill|1978|en|1978|WD=Q2483|lt=1978}}: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. Mound no longer extant| map=Japan Fukui| type=Round Kofun| map_dot_label=Maruyamazuka Kofun| map_dot_label=top }} '''Maruyamazuka Kofun''' (丸山塚古墳, also known as Maruyama Kofun) was a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Wakasa, Fukui|en|Wakasa, Fukui|WD=Q1349039|lt=Wakasa Town|1=Wakasa, Fukui}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|en|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|WD=Q1204541|lt=Mikatakaminaka District|1=Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|en|Fukui Prefecture|WD=Q133879|lt=Fukui Prefecture|1=Fukui Prefecture}}, Japan. It was a round tumulus that typeed part of the {{ill|Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja|上中古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami-naka Kofun Cluster|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (including the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster). Designated as a town historic site under the name "Maruyama Kofun," its excavated burial goods are also recognized as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was the largest round tumulus in the Wakasa region but has since been lost. == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Major Kofun in the Kami-naka Cluster !Cluster!!name!!type!!Length of Mound!!built |- |Wakibukuro||{{ill|Jōnozuka Kofun|en|Jōnozuka Kofun|WD=Q17993480|lt=Jōnozuka Kofun|1=Jōnozuka Kofun}}||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}||100 m||Early 5th century |- | ||Shiroyama Kofun||Zenpō-kōen-fun||63 m||Mid 5th century |- |rowspan=2|Wakibukuro||{{ill|Nishizuka Kofun|en|Nishizuka Kofun|WD=Q18337677|lt=Nishizuka Kofun|1=Nishizuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||74 m||Late 5th century |- |{{ill|Nakatsuka Kofun|ja|中塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuka Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||72 m||Late 5th century |- |Tentokuji||{{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||68 m||Early 6th century |- |rowspan=2|Hikasa||{{ill|Kamifunazuka Kofun|en|Kamifunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17990214|lt=Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun|1=Kamifuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||70 m||Early 6th century |- |{{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|1=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}||Zenpō-kōen-fun||85 m||Mid 6th century |- |Tentokuji||'''Maruyamazuka Kofun'''||Round Kofun||50 m||Mid 6th century |}
The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River|en|Kita River|WD=Q11401571|lt=Kita River (Fukui)|1=Kita River}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}} or {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|1=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}, the last {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kingship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * {{ill|1953|en|1953|WD=Q18585|lt=1953|1=1953}}: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * {{ill|1955|en|1955|WD=Q18577|lt=1955|1=1955}}: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * {{ill|1957|en|1957|WD=Q5311|lt=1957|1=1957}}: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * {{ill|1978|en|1978|WD=Q2483|lt=1978|1=1978}}: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast. The Maruyamazuka Kofun was a large round tumulus constructed on the left bank of the {{ill|Kita River|en|Kita River|WD=Q11401571|lt=Kita River (Fukui)|1=Kita River}} in southwestern Fukui Prefecture, central Wakasa region. Located 250 meters south of the {{ill|Jūzen no Mori Kofun|ja|十善の森古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūzen no Mori Kofun|qq=}}, it typeed part of the Tentokuji Kofun Cluster. In 1957, the tumulus was destroyed during restoration work following flooding caused by the North River’s levee breach, though its stone chamber was investigated beforehand. The mound was circular, measuring approximately 50 meters in diameter and 10 meters in height, and was constructed in two tiers{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. No traces of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}} or {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} were identified on its surface{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The tumulus featured a 20-meter-wide moat surrounding the base{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southeast{{Sfn|Maruyamazuka Kofun (Ancient Kofun)|1989}}. Measuring 6 meters for the burial chamber and 11 meters for the entrance passage, the large stone chamber had been looted but yielded numerous grave goods during the investigation. Constructed in the mid-6th century, the Maruyamazuka Kofun is considered to have been built after the {{ill|Shimofunazuka Kofun|en|Shimofunazuka Kofun|WD=Q17992906|lt=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun|1=Shimofuna Tsuka Kofun}}, the last {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} in the region. Its transition from zenpō-kōen-fun to round tumuli represents the period when the leadership's burial practices shifted. This change, marked by the construction of large stone chambers, is seen across Japan, and the early adoption in the Wakasa region reflects its close ties to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kingship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2658252}}Permanent Exhibit Catalogue, Wakasa Mikata Jomon Museum and Wakasa Town History and Culture Museum, 2014.. == Archaeological History == * {{ill|1953|en|1953|WD=Q18585|lt=1953|1=1953}}: Severe flooding caused by Typhoon No. 13, leading to the collapse of the North River levee. * {{ill|1955|en|1955|WD=Q18577|lt=1955|1=1955}}: Designated as a historic site by the typeer Kami-naka Town on December 6 (now Historic Site1 by Wakasa Town). * {{ill|1957|en|1957|WD=Q5311|lt=1957|1=1957}}: Stone chamber investigated and subsequently destroyed during flood restoration works. The mound was flattened. * {{ill|1978|en|1978|WD=Q2483|lt=1978|1=1978}}: burial goods excavated from the kofun were Historic Site1 as Fukui Prefecture Historic Site on July 25. == burial == The burial facility was a one-sided {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southeast.
